questions.question: Why is the media often called the "Fourth Estate"?
options: It acts as an essential check on power alongside the three branches of government
It is the fourth branch of the army
It is part of the judiciary
questions.explanation: The media is called the Fourth Estate because a free press is an essential check on power alongside the executive, legislative and judicial branches.

questions.question: What is "watchdog journalism"?
options: Investigative reporting that holds the powerful accountable
questions.explanation: Watchdog journalism scrutinises those in power and exposes wrongdoing, as in the Watergate investigation.

questions.question: Which investigation led to the resignation of US President Richard Nixon?
questions.explanation: The Washington Post's Watergate investigation (1972-74) led to President Nixon's resignation.

questions.question: Who developed the concept of the "public sphere"?
questions.explanation: The German philosopher Jürgen Habermas developed the concept of the public sphere as a space for democratic deliberation.

questions.question: What does "agenda-setting" describe?
options: How media shapes public priorities by choosing which topics to cover
questions.explanation: Agenda-setting describes how the media shapes public priorities by deciding which topics receive coverage.
